price_per_million.source: copied from reasoning_models_v1 (confirmed 2026-11-11); thinking tokens billed as output

research_concepts: opponent next-possession PPP after a play type (defensive aftershock)
play-type label construction and foul-ending artifacts
conditioning on outcome of play X
methodological_questions: Is the opponent next-possession PPP shift after X play-type-specific, or a generic effect of the previous possession ending (dead ball, made basket, score)?
Is the between-play-type spread in aftershock large enough to change any AVOID label, given label thresholds and uncertainty?
Do own-sequence lags have detectable effects given the small number of own-next pairs?
Does conditioning on X success or on outcome-derived labels create leakage or an artifact?
How to handle confounding from game state, lineups, possession-ending type and foul endings, and how to control multiplicity across play types?

historical_evidence.finding: Sequential pair premium and defensive aftershock. In APPA-049 the aftershock replicates for 8/8 play types in all-games and playoffs (e.g. CUT +0.119 n=21,398; TRANSITION +0.135 n=26,262; playoffs CUT +0.131 n=1,145, TRANSITION +0.126 n=1,529) on n=458,604 opponent possessions. Top pair premiums: PUTBACK->TRANSITION +0.084 n=565; CUT->PULL_UP +0.065 n=2,620. APPS-037 reports the all-games aftershock after success as +0.119 to +0.135 across play types (opponent scores about 1.07-1.09 vs a 1.206 baseline). Own-next (A1) was treated as exploratory (~4% of pairs; baseline 0.975 PPP, n=18,943). APPS-037 is verdict 'descriptive', failure type E_unclear. The record flags the aftershock as possibly a generic dead-ball/score effect rather than play-type-specific. The record also notes tiny-n team cells marked significant at |t|>=2, and an opposite sign convention from the 52-series net-swing table where DRIVE/POST_UP have negative net swing. Validation is same_pipeline only, auto_limited_by LIM:small_sample, and 'members disagree' is flagged yes.

Play-type labeling audit: OTHER has 36% foul endings with inflated PPP (FOUL_BUCKET). DRIVE is 12pp below the foul benchmark (FOUL_LEAK). PNR shows a 22% foul rate. Only 335 of 50,668 possessions (0.7%) map to a real play type via initiation_type. Verdict: artifact_found; no validation recorded.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Reading play-type PPP differences as pure efficiency without accounting for foul-ending labelling; initiation_type mapping as a source of play-type labels
failed_approaches.why: C_artifact: foul endings inflate or deflate PPP by play type (OTHER, DRIVE, PNR), and initiation_type maps only 0.7% of possessions, so it is not usable for labelling.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Interpreting a uniform positive aftershock (8/8 play types, similar magnitude) as play-type-specific disruption, and treating own-next lags as a tested effect
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as E_unclear for APPS-037: the uniform effect may be a generic dead-ball/score effect. Own-next was only exploratory (~4% of pairs), and the family is limited by LIM:small_sample with only same-pipeline validation.

evidence_establishes: FAM:SF07 (status supported): the opponent's next-possession PPP after a team's successful play type X is about 0.12-0.135 below the opponent-next baseline (1.206) for all 8 play types, in all-games and playoffs, at large n (per-play-type n=5.9k-57.6k).
FAM:SF07: the spread of aftershock across play types is narrow (+0.119 to +0.135) as recorded.
FAM:SF07: own-next (A1) pairs are rare (~4% of pairs, n=18,943), so own-sequence lag estimates rest on few observations.
FAM:SF-CHT-025 (status artifact): play-type labels and PPP are contaminated by foul endings, and initiation_type is not a viable label source (0.7% mapped).
evidence_does_not_establish: That the aftershock is large enough to drive or change AVOID labels. No retrieved record links aftershock magnitude to label assignment or label flips.
That the aftershock is play-type-specific rather than a generic effect of the preceding possession ending.
That own-sequence lags matter. They were exploratory only, and no adequately powered result is recorded.
Whether the aftershock survives conditioning on possession-ending type (make, miss, turnover, foul), score, clock and lineup. Validation was same-pipeline only.
Anything about the 2025-26 playoffs, which are incomplete as of the question date.
own_inferences: Because the aftershock is nearly uniform across play types, it should shift all labels together and cannot by itself separate play types into AVOID vs non-AVOID. Only the differential aftershock (about 0.016 spread across play types in the record) could move relative labels, and that is small against the SEs of the smaller play types.

Conditioning on X 'success' (a made basket) forces the opponent to inbound against a set defense, which mechanically lowers opponent-next PPP relative to a baseline that includes live-ball transition after misses and turnovers. This makes the uniform ~0.12 aftershock likely a possession-ending-type composition effect (CONFOUNDING and OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL).
Using 'success' of X to define a label is not knowable at decision time, so any prospective AVOID rule must use ex-ante features.

Rough power under an assumed possession-points SD of ~1.2: SE for a play-type mean with n≈5.9k is ~0.016, with n≈50k ~0.005. The MDE for a between-play-type difference is ~0.05 for the smallest play types and ~0.02 for the largest. Own-next cells with n of hundreds to ~2k have MDE ~0.1-0.15, so only very large own-sequence effects are detectable.
The foul-ending artifact in SF-CHT-025 probably also contaminates next-possession PPP, since foul-ending possessions are followed by dead-ball restarts.
uncertainties: The operational definition and threshold of the AVOID label are not given in the task or records, so 'large enough' is unquantified.
'H2 baseline' is not defined in the retrieved records, and whether the 1.206 baseline is conditioned or unconditional is unclear.
The sign convention conflicts with the 52-series net-swing table. 'Members disagree: yes' is flagged although adjudication was rule-based.
I did not retrieve related families (FAM:SF-APPA-050, FAM:SF-APPS-049, FAM:SF40), which may bear on label thresholds.
2025-26 playoff data are partial before 2026-06-21, and the prior numbers were produced on 2026-05-31 with an unknown data vintage.
Whether the possession table identifies the previous possession's ending type reliably enough to adjust for it.

historical_effect.explanation: Without history I might have treated this as a simple descriptive test. SF07 shows the raw aftershock effect is already established as large and uniform, and the open issues are specificity and label impact. SF07 also flags a possible generic dead-ball effect and exploratory-only own-next lags. SF-CHT-025 shows labelling artifacts such as foul endings. I therefore moved from 'proceed' to proceed_with_changes: reframe to the differential (play-type-specific) aftershock net of possession-ending type, test label flips directly, add foul and ending-type controls, and treat own-sequence lags as a low-power secondary question.

blocking_constraints.text: Own-next pairs are only ~4% of pairs (n=18,943 overall), so per-play-type own-sequence lag effects are detectable only if very large (MDE roughly 0.1-0.15 PPP); smaller play types are also low-powered for differential aftershock.

AVOID threshold is undefined in the task, and play-type labelling has documented foul-ending artifacts and 0.7% initiation_type mapping; label flips cannot be evaluated until a frozen label rule is specified.

prior_work.summary: The existence and size of the opponent next-possession aftershock (~0.12-0.135, 8/8 play types, replicated in playoffs) is recorded as supported in FAM:SF07. Its play-type specificity, its sufficiency to drive AVOID labels, and own-sequence lag effects are not established. Labelling artifacts from fouls are recorded in FAM:SF-CHT-025.

risks.text: Aftershock is conditioned on X success. Possession-ending type, made vs missed shot, foul endings, score margin, clock, period, lineup, opponent strength and home court all affect the next opponent possession and are not balanced across play types.
'Success' and label definitions depend on the outcome of X, and PPP-based AVOID labels are derived from the same outcomes used to estimate the aftershock.
Foul endings distort PPP by play type (OTHER 36%, PNR 22%, DRIVE 12pp below benchmark), and initiation_type maps only 0.7% of possessions.
Any prospective AVOID rule using whether X succeeded, or the following possession, uses information unavailable at decision time.
Own-next pairs are ~4% of pairs; small play types (PUTBACK n=5.9k) and pair cells (n=565) and team cells (n=16-18) are underpowered or unreliable.
8 play types x pair combinations x team cells x all-games/playoffs; prior notes show |t|>=2 flagged on tiny cells without correction.
The uniform aftershock may be a generic effect, so a result is interpretable only against placebo comparisons (e.g. lag-2 possessions, matched non-play-type endings).
Possession segmentation, play-type assignment and previous-possession ending classification come from derived play-by-play and have unquantified error; the baseline definition is unclear.
The 1.206 opponent-next baseline is higher than the own-next baseline 0.975, showing that baseline choice drives the sign and size of the effect.
Pace, spacing and rule or officiating changes across 2022-23 to 2025-26 may shift baselines; playoffs differ from the regular season.

design.estimand: (a) Play-type-specific aftershock: the opponent's next-possession PPP after the team's possession of play type X, minus the opponent's next-possession PPP after a reference possession matched on ending type (make / miss-defensive-rebound / turnover / foul), score margin bin, period, clock bin, lineup-strength proxy and home court. Contrast each X with the pooled mean over play types (differential aftershock). (b) Label impact: the share of play types whose AVOID label (using the frozen rule, applied with and without the aftershock adjustment) changes, with bootstrap CI. (c) Secondary, exploratory: own-next lag effect, the team's next-possession PPP after X vs matched reference.
design.unit: Possession pairs (possession t, immediately following possession t+1), clustered by game; team-level cells are descriptive only.
design.sample: Frozen snapshot of NBA 2022-23, 2023-24 and 2024-25 regular seasons and playoffs, plus 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13). Estimation on 2022-23 to 2024-25; confirmation on 2025-26 regular season. The 2025-26 playoffs are excluded as incomplete before 2026-06-21 and used only as a post-hoc holdout once complete. Exclude garbage time (pre-registered margin/clock rule), end-of-period possessions and possession pairs split by period boundaries. Foul-ending possessions are analysed as a separate stratum and in a sensitivity analysis excluding them.
design.power: Assuming a possession-points SD of ~1.2 (to be verified from data), SE of a play-type mean is ~0.016 (n=5.9k) to ~0.005 (n=50k); the MDE for a between-play-type difference at 80% power, alpha=0.05, is ~0.05 for small play types and ~0.02 for large ones, so the observed 0.016 spread is detectable only among the largest play types. Own-next lag: n=18,943 pairs overall, MDE per play type ~0.1-0.15; only pooled own-lag is primary-eligible, per-play-type own-lag is reported as exploratory. Compute actual power from data before unblinding; if the CI on the differential cannot exclude a label-changing size, report 'inconclusive'.
design.controls: Matching or regression on previous-possession ending type, score margin, period, clock, home court, opponent defensive rating, lineup composition and pace; game-clustered SEs; team and season fixed effects; baseline defined once as the matched-reference PPP, not the 1.206 unconditional baseline. Freeze the AVOID rule (threshold, minimum n, which PPP) before analysis; use only ex-ante features for any prospective label and report success-conditioned estimates as diagnostic only. Resolve the sign convention (positive = opponent scores less) against the 52-series net-swing table.
design.falsification: Placebo 1: lag-2 opponent possession after X should show no aftershock. Placebo 2: randomly permute play-type labels within game and ending-type strata; the differential aftershock should vanish. Placebo 3: after matching on ending type, the uniform ~0.12 aftershock should shrink toward zero if it is a dead-ball composition effect; if it persists at the same size across play types, classify as generic rather than play-type-specific. Replicate in the 2025-26 confirmation sample and in the playoffs. Sensitivity excluding foul endings and OTHER-labelled possessions.
design.multiplicity: Primary family: 8 differential-aftershock contrasts, Holm-corrected at 0.05, plus a single pre-specified label-flip summary. Pair premiums (X->Y), team cells and own-lag per play type are exploratory with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR at 0.10, minimum n=500 per cell (no team cells below that).
design.decision_rule: Supported if (i) at least one play type has a Holm-significant differential aftershock after ending-type matching, replicated in the 2025-26 confirmation sample, with the same sign and an effect of at least the pre-registered label-relevant size, AND (ii) the adjustment flips at least one AVOID label under the frozen rule. Rejected if the CIs exclude label-relevant differences for all play types with adequate power. Artifact if the effect disappears under ending-type matching, permutation placebo or foul exclusion. Otherwise inconclusive. Own-sequence lag claims are reported only as exploratory unless pooled lag is significant and replicated.
design.data_version: Snapshot of NBA stats API per-game files and the derived play-type possession graph database as of a frozen date before analysis (record hashes and the possession-building code version); 2022-23 to 2024-25 complete seasons, 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13), 2025-26 playoffs excluded until complete (2026-06-21). The earlier SF07 numbers (2026-05-31) came from an unknown data vintage, so they are re-derived rather than reused.

methodological_questions: Is the opponent's next-possession PPP after a given play type large enough to change AVOID labels?
Do lagged own-sequence play types (previous possessions by the same team) have meaningful effects on outcomes?
How should confounding by game state, lineup, turnover or live-ball transition, and regression to the mean be handled?
Is there sample size and power for play-type by next-possession estimates, and how to control for multiple testing across play types?
Are play-type labels derived from outcomes, and does this create label leakage or data quality issues?
args.query: Effect of a team's play type on opponent next-possession PPP and own-sequence lags, and whether it is large enough to drive AVOID labels in play-type labeling and data quality

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

messages.content:
Research question (as posed on 2026-06-19, in the area of play-type labeling and data quality):
Opponent next-possession PPP after you run play X is large enough to drive AVOID labels; own-sequence lags similarly matter.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

Stage 1. Reply only with the retrieval call: {"action": "tool", "tool": "retrieve_history", "args": {"research_concepts": ["..."], "methodological_questions": ["..."], "query": "..."}}

reasoning_details.text:
I'm comparing the opponent's next-possession points per possession after a made basket, which runs around 1.07 to 1.09, against the 1.206 baseline, and the 1.206 looks high. I'm checking it against league averages of roughly 1.15 to 1.2, and I suspect the gap comes from conditioning on made baskets, since defenses are set after a score and not in transition after steals or misses.

I'm checking whether a uniform shift in the opponent's next-possession value could really drive the AVOID labels, and it can't: the differences between players are only about 0.016 wide, so any differentiation is tiny. I'm also noting the label artifacts, foul endings, and the own-sequence premium counts, while flagging that the data-date detail and a sign-convention conflict in the net swing table still need sorting out.

I'm settling on proceeding with changes and framing the estimand as the player-specific differential aftershock across the action, adjusting for the outcome of that action, score, period, and clock, along with its effect on label flips. Since the AVOID threshold isn't defined yet, I'll have to pre-register it and run the label check with and without the aftershock adjustment. I'm also assigning rough probabilities to the outcomes and listing the main risks: confounding, outcome-derived labels, label error, and lookahead leakage.

I'm settling on the blocking constraints now: the own-sequence power and the still-unspecified AVOID definition are the ones that matter, and I'm tagging the risks with short codes. I'm also starting the power calculation for the opponent-next points-per-possession estimate, using roughly 1.15 as the per-possession standard deviation.

I'm checking the power for the opponent-next estimate: with a per-possession SD around 1.2, the standard error for the 5,888-possession group is roughly 0.016, and the detectable difference between the two larger groups comes out near 0.02. That means the 0.016 spread between players is only detectable for the large groups, while the small ones are underpowered. The own-sequence cells have wide errors, so only large effects would show up there.

I'm making sure the data window is pinned down: the regular season ended 2026-04-13, the 2022-23 to 2024-25 playoffs are complete, but the 2025-26 playoffs are still running until 2026-06-21, so I'd keep those out of the primary analysis or hold them back as a check, with a snapshot hash. I'm also noting that the earlier "H2" baseline is never defined, so I can't tell what period it covered and should mention that uncertainty.
